name: News/Earnings Gapper

card.context: A fresh, named catalyst released outside market hours, most often a report, on a liquid stock that is not already up 30% in three months, above the 200-day by the close. Earnings season, Green or Yellow market, often as a correction ends.
card.pattern: The open is 4% or more above the prior close on at least 3 times average volume. The gap holds: the day never trades back to the prior close, closes green and in the upper half of its range. Best out of a base.
card.trigger: PREV DAY HIGH BREAK: within 2 to 10 sessions, after a pullback of two down days or an inside day whose closes all hold the gap-day low, a market buy as price trades over the prior day's high. Day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form.
card.stop: A few cents under the pullback low; on day one, under the day's low at the buy, usually the opening-range low. Skip a day-one stop more than 1.5 ATR away.
card.failure_mode: The gap fills or closes red (a News Failure), or the stock closes under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions. The pullback buy fails most when the reclaim comes early after a very wide day-one bar on a stock already extended.

criteria.statement: The family lesson: any catalyst gap, earnings or news, traded on day one or on its first pullback and reclaim within about 10 sessions. The Episodic Pivot (the neglected name) and the Power Earnings Gap (the leader out of a base) are the two traded units; this card teaches the pullback-and-reclaim entry for both.

measure.what: sessions from the gap day to the entry

criteria.evidence: The register's default (D-002): EP and PEG are the two traded units and News Gapper is the family lesson that teaches the first-pullback-and-reclaim entry for both.

criteria.statement: A gap that fades on day one and gets going days later (the owner's U, RDDT, ESTC, BFLY and ELVN; Bonde's delayed reaction EP) is a named variant inside the gap family, not its own lesson.

criteria.statement: The gap holds on day one: the day closes above the prior close, never trades back to it, and closes in the upper half of its range. A close in the lower half is a B-; a red close is not this setup.

criteria.statement: Prefer a gap out of a base: an open above the top of a base of 4 weeks or more, or out of a quiet range where the prior 60 sessions' high is no more than 35% above their low.

ng.volume_a_plus: the highest volume in a year or ever; the average daily volume in the first 15 to 20 minutes
ng.gap_holds: a close in the top quarter of the range
ng.base_before: opens above a base of 4 weeks or more, or out of a 3 to 6 month quiet range; above a rising 200-day
ng.not_late: quiet before the gap, not up more than about 15% in 3 months

ng.stop_day1: a day-one stop within about 1 ATR and near 3%
ng.entry_pullback: the first pullback holds the upper half of the gap day

ng.gap_holds: a close in the lower half

ng.not_late: up 30% or more already; a second or third gap
ng.market_reading: a weak group; a Yellow market (smaller and fewer)
ng.entry_pullback: the pullback dips under the gap-day midpoint

lookalikes.tell: Measure the gap and look at the six months before it. An EP is the biggest-surprise version: 10% or more, the first in six months, on a neglected name. A gapper of 4% to 10%, or on a stock that was not neglected, is taught here.

Check the earnings database. If the gap day is a report's reaction day on an established leader clearing its base, it is the PEG; a gap on any other headline, or the first-pullback entry on either, is taught here.

Look at the day before. A Kicker needs a weak red close and then a gap of only 1.5% or more on positioning, rarely a headline; a News Gapper opens 4% or more on a named catalyst with 3 times volume, and the day before can be any color.
Read the close. A gapper holds its gap and closes green in the upper half; a News Failure gaps up on good news and closes red, under the prior close. Same headline, opposite trade.

Count the sessions and look at where the low lands. The gapper's pullback stays above the gap-day low and reclaims within 10 sessions; Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low itself, 2 to 60 sessions on, bought as that low is defended.

invalidations: Day one closes red, or trades back to the prior close; a red close after good news is the News Failure (ng.inv_red_close).
A close under the gap-day low in the first 10 sessions (ng.inv_close_under_low).
The pullback breaks the gap-day low before any reclaim: no Buy 2 (ng.inv_pullback_breaks_low).
After the 10-session window the chart is its own later setup: Gap Support, Slingshot, Go Signal, HVE (ng.scope).
Still under 1R after 10 trading days: sell (ng.time_stop).
After entry: the stop is the exit; no porosity, it only moves up (ng.no_porosity).
mistakes: Buying a gap with no catalyst, or a weak one: an upgrade, a media mention.
Buying the open before the opening range forms, with no stop to lean on.
Buying a gap that is filling, or that closed red.
Buying the third gap of a parabolic burst (Bracco's climax gap; ChartSchool's exhaustion gap).
Sizing from a tight intraday stop as if a news stock cannot gap again (the owner's FSLY).
Calling every big gap earnings without checking: a quarter are not.
Calling an earnings gap a Kicker.
Holding through the next report without a 5R cushion.
Moving the stop under the gap-day low to give it room.
Chasing a gap far above the opening-range high, or a stretched later entry.

short_mirror.note: The earnings breakdown (dossier 8.6), the owner's own word for the down version, kept apart from the bear gap off the highs: a gap down of 4% or more on bad earnings or news, on 3 times volume, closing in the lower half, in a stock already under its 200-day (B26) with RS 20 or less (C31 mirror); short at market under the opening-range low; stop a few cents over the day's high; skip if hard to borrow (D48). Bulkowski's bad surprise: a quick but shallow decline, almost half bottom in one week, so take trims faster. Whether to teach it is D-001; the dossier's proposal.

best_conditions: A Green or Yellow market reading. Earnings season, when the gaps cluster in 3 to 4 weeks each quarter. Coming out of a correction, when the recent ER gappers lead and Bonde finds 50 to 100 opportunities in a season.

question_seeds.seed: What is the smallest opening gap for a News Gapper, and what size makes it an A+?
Describe the first-pullback-and-reclaim entry: how many sessions, what the closes must hold, and what triggers the buy.
On a day-one buy, where does the stop go, and when is it too wide?
Hidden ticker, six sessions after a gap: tap the day the pullback reclaims the prior day's high and the low the stop sits under.
Hidden ticker: four gap days. Which ones held the gap, never trading back to the prior close and closing in the upper half?
Hidden ticker: the pullback is in. Did any close break the gap-day low? Take Buy 2 or pass.
News Gapper or PEG: the gap day is a report reaction day on a leader clearing a four-month base. Which lesson owns the day, and which owns the pullback?
News Gapper or News Failure: a contract headline, an 8% gap, and a close 2% under the prior close. Which is it?
News Gapper or Kicker: a weak red close, a 2% gap on 1.6x volume, no headline. Which is it?
News Gapper or Gap Support: five weeks after the gap, price tests the gap-up low and holds it. Which trade is this?

Day 7 after the gap closes under the gap-day low. You have not bought yet. What now?
Two 11% gaps on record volume: one on a stock flat for three months, one on a stock up 24% in three months. Grade each as a Buy 2.
Same gap, two closes: one at 93% of the range, one at 40%. Grade each.
A 6% gap on an analyst upgrade against a 6% gap on a government contract, both on 4x volume. Grade the catalyst of each.
Prior close 180.00, open 187.90. How big is the gap, and does it clear the floor?
Low 100.00, high 110.00, close 107.00. Where in the range did the day close, and is that the upper half?

conflicts: Sources are cited by the validator's positional numbering of the dossier's section 11 (S1 is the first source in reading order, counting table body rows and top-level bullets); the dossier itself prints no ids.

Scope against its neighbours: this dossier takes any catalyst gap with EP and PEG as named versions; the PEG dossier keeps non-earnings news out of the PEG; the register's default makes EP and PEG the two traded units and this card the family lesson for the first-pullback-and-reclaim entry (D-002). The card follows the register and flags it.
The gap floor: this dossier 4%, the EP dossier 10%, the PEG dossier 4% plus 0.75 ATR; the owner's TXN example opened 3.7% up. The card takes 4% with 8% preferred and 10% as the A+ (D-033).

The entry: the course draft says never the open, always the reclaim; the owner says he loves trading earnings gappers on day one; the test favours day one on earnings gaps (36.6% / 24.4% on real hourly bars against 28.9% / 19.2% for the pullback). The card teaches both, day one first (D-086).

C29 on day one: 16 of the owner's 18 named gaps closed more than 10% above the 10-day; applied on day one it removes most of his favourite trades and does not remove worse ones. The card recommends exempting the gap day (D-017); the PEG card recommends applying it, which is why the PEG's default entry is the pause.

A13 on day one: the stop under the gap day's low was over 3% on 52.5% of earnings gaps from the close. The card allows up to 1.5 ATR (Kullamägi's cap) pending the owner (D-005); the EP card skips past 3%.
Which news counts: Bonde's high and low probability lists and Kullamägi's types against upgrades, index additions and sympathy moves; the register's default grades the latter lower (D-032).
